history.period: Mythological; developed as a landscaped park in modern times
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. Agnigarh is a small hillock on the bank of the Brahmaputra at Tezpur, developed as a garden/park and viewpoint, not a functioning temple. 'Agnigarh' (Agni = fire, garh = fortress) is the legendary 'fortress of fire' built by the asura king Banasura to keep his daughter Usha in isolation; the hill is the setting of the Usha-Aniruddha love story and the Hari-Hara battle between Krishna and Shiva that gave Tezpur ('city of blood') its name. The hilltop has a circular stairway, stone sculptures depicting the legend and the Krishna-Shiva battle, and a viewing platform with panoramas of the Brahmaputra and Tezpur town. No temple deity, idol, or worship tradition is documented for the hill itself (the nearby Mahabhairab and Bhairabi temples are separate sites). Coordinates from the Sonitpur district administration listing (26.617736, 92.801841).

name: Agnigarh Hill Temple
town_description: Tezpur, headquarters of Sonitpur district on the north bank of the Brahmaputra about 175 km northeast of Guwahati, is one of Assam's oldest cities and a centre of mythology, archaeology and culture — 'the cultural capital of Assam'.
tradition: Hindu legend/mythology site (hill park); not a temple — no worship tradition documented

travel.railway: Tezpur railway station, about 4 km away
travel.road: On the Brahmaputra bank in Tezpur town; drive to the base, then a short climb up circular steps

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; sunsets over the Brahmaputra are the main draw
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daily 9:00 AM-6:30 PM (per Sonitpur district administration listing)
